question: How much of F's measured fit time is lme4's deriv12 step, which lme4 >= 1.1-38 skips for singular fits, lmer fits with >= 10 covariance parameters, glmer fits with >= 20 parameters and fits with >= 1e4 rows?
result: 2x2 maximal lmer (20 theta, all fits singular): 0.725 vs 0.392 s at 384 rows (3 pairs, medians), 3.70 vs 1.47 s at 1,536 (2 pairs), 23.3 vs 8.4 s at 6,144 (1 pair); identical REML criteria. glmer 2x2 maximal: 10.55 vs 9.46 s (384), 44.1 vs 37.0 s (1,536). One-factor crossed lmer 1,536 rows: 0.114 vs 0.070 s (derivs still computed in lme4 2.x when non-singular). F's extrapolated 23 s at 6,144 rows confirmed (23.3 s).
bearing_on_F: F-E02 numbers confirmed; F-E04/F-E16 central figures overstate current-lme4 cost of 2x2 maximal fits by 1.9-2.8x; the H1 cap loses its cost rationale

question: Does F's pilot (Bartlett across clusters on raw conditional residuals) test what catalogue L5-03 predicts (spurious heteroscedasticity across cluster sizes)?
result: Correct model, 500 reps per cell, nominal .05. F pilot cell (J40 m5 CV .5): Bartlett by cluster .040, Brown-Forsythe by size stratum raw .068, studentised .058. J40 sizes 2/5/20/50 ICC .3: .032 / .092 / .056. ICC .5: .054 / .146 / .080. J100 ICC .3: .034 / .182 / .054 (MCSE .008-.017).
bearing_on_F: Refutes F's inference that L5-03's inflation 'needs more extreme cells': it appears in moderate unbalanced designs once the comparison is by cluster size; studentising removes most of it
